recorded.env: POLYTRACE_SYNC=1 (dumps on), POLYTRACE_OUT=<file>; no other variable
recorded.logger: tools/wintrace/polytrace-sync (spec-chrome-win-3 version: caller module+offset, argument classes, out-buffer dumps)
recorded.registry_state: cold: before every run HKCU\Software\Chrome for Testing and HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome for Testing did not exist (the state of a machine that never ran Chrome for Testing, and of Poly's registry at start); Chrome made them during the run

window.from: process start (the first call chrome_elf.dll makes through its imports)
window.to: the first AddVectoredExceptionHandler (the end of chrome_elf's crash-reporting initialisation)

how_to_compare: Run the same kit on Poly (chrome-win run --kit chrome_elf.dll,chrome.exe) and read polytrace.jsonl as this file's `calls`:
call n of Poly's sequence (after dropping `ignored_functions`) must be the same function (`fn`) from the same caller (`at`,
module+offset of the return address); `args`/`ret`/`out` are then compared field by field after the same normalisation
(classes instead of values, `<-n` = the value call n returned or wrote). `<var>` fields differ between Windows runs and are not compared.
The first call where Poly's `fn`/`at` differs, or where a class/link/status/out value differs, is the first divergence.
machine_facts: out sysinfo (cpus, mask, revision), QueryPerformanceFrequency's u64, GetCommandLine* (paths normalised)
are this machine's; they are in the file because Chrome reads them, not because Poly must equal them

landmarks.what: the delay-load helper loads the advapi32 proxy; GetProcAddress at +0x158e0a resolves each delay-loaded name

Poly's S1 stops after this call: access violation reading [0x10] in the code that follows (leaf +0x8e9b4, called from +0x8e2a1, rcx = 0). On Windows the first thing after it is AcquireSRWLockExclusive at +0x1580a6, then GetProcAddress(advapi32 proxy, ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW).
